title.raw: 卷76 盧同 張烈 Volume 76: Lu Tong, Zhang Lie

sentences.zh: 盧同 張烈

translations.literal: Lu Tong; Zhang Lie
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong; Zhang Lie

sentences.zh: 盧同，字叔倫，范陽涿人，盧玄之族孫。

translations.literal: Lu Tong, style name Shulun, was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang, a clan grandson of Lu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong, whose style name was Shulun, came from Zhuo in Fanyang and was a descendant of Lu Xuan's clan.

sentences.zh: 父輔，字顯元，本州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Fu, style name Xianyuan, was Separate Carriage of this province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu, styled Xianyuan, served as provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 同身長八尺，容貌魁偉，善於處世。

translations.literal: Tong was eight chi in height, his appearance imposing and grand, and skilled in dealing with the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tong stood eight chi tall, with a towering presence, and was adept in worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 太和中，起家北海王詳國常侍。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he first entered service as a household retainer of the state of Prince Xiang of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe reign he began his career as a household attendant in the household of Prince Xiang of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司空祭酒、昌黎太守。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Libationer of the Minister of Works and Grand Administrator of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Libationer of the Works and Grand Administrator of Changli.

sentences.zh: 尋為營州長史，仍帶郡。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he became Chief Clerk of Ying Province, still holding the commandery as well.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Chief Clerk of Yingzhou, retaining concurrent charge of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 入除河南尹丞，遷太尉屬。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Assistant to the Intendant of Henan, then transferred to an aide post under the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital as Assistant Intendant of Henan, then promoted to an aide under the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 會豫州城民白早生反，都督中山王英、尚書邢巒等討之，詔同為軍司。

translations.literal: It happened that the city people of Yuzhou, Bai Zaosheng, rebelled; the Commander-in-Chief Prince Ying of Zhongshan, the Minister Xing Luan, and others attacked them, and an edict appointed Tong as Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: When the townspeople of Yuzhou under Bai Zaosheng rose in revolt, Prince Ying of Zhongshan as commander-in-chief, Minister Xing Luan, and others marched against them; Tong was ordered to serve as army aide.

sentences.zh: 事平，除冀州鎮東府長史。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Eastern Pacification Headquarters in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, he was made Chief Clerk of the Eastern Pacification headquarters in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂解任。

translations.literal: He met with his father's bereavement and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 後除司空諮議參軍，兼司馬，為營構東宮都將。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Consulting Army Aide to the Minister of Works, concurrently Major, and made Chief Commander for constructing the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Consulting Army Aide under the Minister of Works, also serving as Major, and named chief commander for building the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，秦州民反，詔同兼通直常侍，持節慰諭之，多所降下。

translations.literal: In the Yan-chang era the people of Qinzhou rebelled; an edict made Tong concurrently Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, bearing credentials to console and instruct them, and many submitted.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yan-chang era, when the people of Qinzhou rebelled, Tong was ordered to serve concurrently as Regular Attendant and, bearing imperial credentials, to console and instruct them; many groups surrendered.

sentences.zh: 還轉尚書右丞，進號輔國將軍，以父諱不拜，改授龍驤。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, advanced in title to General Who Assists the State; because of his father's taboo name he did not accept the appointment and was instead given Dragon Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he became Right Assistant Director in the Masters of Writing and was advanced to General Who Assists the State; because the title conflicted with his father's name he declined it and was reassigned as Dragon Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，轉左丞，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiping era he was transferred to Left Assistant Director and given the additional title General Who Captures the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xiping reign he was moved to Left Assistant Director and additionally named General Who Captures the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 時相州刺史奚康生徵民歲調，皆七八十尺，以邀奉公之譽。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Xi Kangsheng, levied the people's annual tribute in lengths all of seventy or eighty chi, to win a reputation for devoted public service.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xi Kangsheng, Inspector of Xiangzhou, collected the annual levy from the people in bolts of seventy or eighty chi each, seeking a reputation for scrupulous devotion to the state.

sentences.zh: 部內患之，同於歲祿官給長絹。

translations.literal: Those within his jurisdiction were distressed by this; Tong, in the year's salary, had officials issue long bolts of silk as stipends.
translations.idiomatic: The people under his jurisdiction resented this; Tong, from the year's official salary, had long bolts of silk issued as stipends.

sentences.zh: 同乃舉按康生度外徵調。

translations.literal: Tong thereupon brought charges and investigated Kangsheng's levies beyond the prescribed measure.
translations.idiomatic: Tong then impeached Kangsheng for collecting levies beyond the statutory quota.

sentences.zh: 書奏，詔科康生之罪，兼褒同在公之績。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, an edict assessed Kangsheng's crime and also praised Tong's public achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict convicted Kangsheng and at the same time commended Tong's service to the public good.

sentences.zh: 肅宗世，朝政稍衰，人多竊冒軍功。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Suzong, court governance gradually declined, and many people usurped military merit fraudulently.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Suzong's reign, court governance weakened, and many men fraudulently claimed military merit.

sentences.zh: 同閱吏部勳書，因加檢覆，覈得竊階者三百餘人。

translations.literal: Tong reviewed the Ministry of Personnel's merit records and, adding further inspection and verification, found more than three hundred who had stolen ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Tong examined the Ministry of Personnel's merit registers and, on further audit, identified more than three hundred who had stolen rank.

sentences.zh: 同乃表言：

translations.literal: Tong thereupon submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tong then memorialized the throne as follows:

sentences.zh: 竊見吏部勳簿，多皆改換。

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that the Ministry of Personnel's merit registers have for the most part been altered and replaced.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that the Ministry's merit registers have largely been altered or replaced.

sentences.zh: 乃校中兵奏按，並復乖舛。

translations.literal: When they were checked against the Central Army's submitted investigations, they were again at variance.
translations.idiomatic: When checked against the Central Army bureau's submitted investigations, they again failed to agree.

sentences.zh: 臣聊爾揀練，已得三百餘人，明知隱而未露者，動有千數。

translations.literal: Your subject, in a cursory sorting and review, has already found more than three hundred; those plainly hidden and not yet exposed must number in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In a preliminary review I have already found more than three hundred cases; those still concealed must number in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 愚謂罪雖恩免，猶須刊定。

translations.literal: This fool believes that although the crimes may be forgiven by grace, they still must be corrected and fixed in the record.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that even if offenses are pardoned by imperial grace, the records must still be corrected.

sentences.zh: 請遣一都令史與令僕省事各一人，總集吏部、中兵二局勳簿，對勾奏按。

translations.literal: I request that one chief clerk and one secretariat aide from the Masters of Writing and Works be dispatched to gather together the merit registers of the Ministry of Personnel and the Central Army bureaus and cross-check them against submitted investigations.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that one chief clerk and one secretariat aide each be sent to assemble the merit registers of the Personnel and Central Army bureaus and cross-check them against the submitted investigations.

sentences.zh: 若名級相應者，即於黃素楷書大字，具件階級數，令本曹尚書以朱印印之。

translations.literal: Where names and ranks correspond, then on yellow plain silk write in large regular script the full list of rank levels, and have the Minister of that bureau affix a vermilion seal.
translations.idiomatic: Where name and rank match, let the full rank and grade be written in large characters on yellow plain silk and sealed in vermilion by the responsible minister.

sentences.zh: 明造兩通，一關吏部，一留兵局，與奏按對掌。

translations.literal: Clearly make two copies: one to be filed with the Ministry of Personnel, one kept in the military bureau, each to be held against the submitted investigations.
translations.idiomatic: Two copies should be made explicitly: one filed with Personnel, one kept in the military bureau, each held against the investigation records.

sentences.zh: 進則防揩洗之偽，退則無改易之理。

translations.literal: Going forward this will guard against the fraud of erasure and alteration; looking back, there will be no grounds for changing records.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth erasure and forgery will be prevented; retroactive alteration will no longer be possible.

sentences.zh: 從前以來，勳書上省，唯列姓名，不載本屬，致令竊濫之徒輕為苟且。

translations.literal: From former times until now, when merit documents were sent up to the province, only names were listed and native jurisdictions were not recorded, causing those who stole and abused rank to treat the matter lightly and carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Hitherto merit documents sent to the capital listed only names, not home jurisdictions, so that fraudsters treated the system casually.

sentences.zh: 今請征職白民，具列本州、郡、縣、三長之所；

translations.literal: Now I request that for commoners called to service, their original province, commandery, county, and the locality of the three chiefs be fully listed;
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter, for commoners drafted to service, let their home province, commandery, county, and ward under the three-chief system be fully listed;

sentences.zh: 其實官正職者，亦列名貫，別錄歷階。

translations.literal: for those who are actual officials in regular posts, also list their name and lineage, and separately record their successive ranks.
translations.idiomatic: and for men holding actual regular office, let name and lineage be listed and successive ranks recorded separately.

sentences.zh: 仰本軍印記其上，然後印縫各上所司，統將、都督並皆印記，然後列上行臺。

translations.literal: Have the home army stamp and seal upon it, then at the seal seam submit copies to each responsible office; the commanding general and regional inspector shall all affix seals, and only then submit the list to the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Let the home army affix its seal first; then, with seals along the fold, copies should go to each responsible office, and the army commander and regional inspector should all seal them before the list is sent to the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 行臺關太尉，太尉檢練精實，乃始關刺省重究括，然後奏申。

translations.literal: The mobile headquarters forwards it to the Grand Commandant; the Grand Commandant inspects, refines, and verifies the facts, and only then forwards it to the province for thorough re-examination, after which it is memorialized and reported.
translations.idiomatic: The mobile headquarters forwards it to the Grand Commandant; once he has verified the facts, it goes to the provincial authorities for thorough review, and only then is it memorialized to the throne.

sentences.zh: 奏出之日，黃素朱印，關付吏部。

translations.literal: On the day the memorial is issued, yellow plain silk with vermilion seal is forwarded to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the memorial is approved, a yellow register sealed in vermilion is forwarded to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 頃來非但偷階冒名，改換勳簿而已，或一階再取，或易名受級，凡如此者，其人不少。

translations.literal: Recently it is not only stealing ranks and usurping names and altering merit registers; some take one rank twice, or change names to receive grades—such cases are not few.
translations.idiomatic: Recently men have not only stolen rank and usurped names or altered merit registers; some have claimed the same rank twice, or changed names to receive grades—such cases are numerous.

sentences.zh: 良由吏部無簿，防塞失方。

translations.literal: This is truly because the Ministry of Personnel has no register, and the means of prevention and blocking have failed.
translations.idiomatic: This is chiefly because Personnel keeps no proper register, so safeguards have failed.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 吏部加階之後，簿不注記，緣此之故，易生僥倖。

translations.literal: After the Ministry of Personnel adds a rank, the register is not annotated; because of this, opportunism easily arises.
translations.idiomatic: After Personnel awards a rank, the register is not annotated, and opportunism easily follows.

sentences.zh: 自今敍階之後，名簿具注加補日月，尚書印記，然後付曹。

translations.literal: From now on, after ranks are conferred, the name register shall fully note the date of addition and supplementation, the Minister shall affix a seal, and only then hand it to the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever a rank is conferred, the register must note the date of the award, be sealed by the minister, and only then passed to the bureau.

sentences.zh: 郎中別作抄目，[1]印記一如尚書，郎中自掌，遞代相付。

translations.literal: The director shall make a separate copy register, stamped like the Minister's register, which the director keeps in hand and passes on in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau director shall keep a separate copy register, stamped like the minister's copy, held in his own custody and handed on in rotation.

sentences.zh: 此制一行，差止姦罔。

translations.literal: Once this system is implemented, fraud and deception will largely cease.
translations.idiomatic: Once this system is in force, fraud will largely cease.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 同又奏曰：

translations.literal: Tong again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tong submitted a further memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣頃奏以黃素為勳，[2]具注官名、戶屬及吏部換勳之法，事目三條，已蒙旨許。

translations.literal: Your subject recently memorialized using yellow plain silk for merit records, fully noting official names, household affiliation, and the Ministry of Personnel's method for altering merit records—three items in all—which have already received imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: I recently proposed using yellow registers for merit records, with full notation of office, household affiliation, and Personnel's rules for altering registers—three measures in all—which Your Majesty has already approved.

sentences.zh: 臣伏思黃素勳簿，政可粗止姦偽，然在軍虛詐，猶未可盡。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that yellow plain silk merit registers can roughly stop fraud and forgery, yet false claims in the army still cannot be fully ended.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that yellow merit registers can curb forgery in general, yet army-side fraud cannot yet be fully eliminated.

sentences.zh: 請自今在軍閱簿之日，行臺、軍司、監軍、都督各明立文按，處處記之。

translations.literal: I request that from now on, on the day of army muster and register review, the mobile headquarters, army aide, army inspector, and regional inspector each clearly establish written records and note every place.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on, on the day registers are reviewed in camp, the mobile headquarters, army aide, army inspector, and regional inspector each keep explicit written records at every point.

sentences.zh: 斬首成一階已上，即令給券。

translations.literal: When decapitations amount to one rank or more, issue a warrant immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever decapitations amount to one full rank of merit or more, a warrant should be issued at once.

sentences.zh: 一紙之上，當中大書起行臺、統軍位號，勳人甲乙。

translations.literal: On a single sheet, write prominently in the center the mobile headquarters and army commander's titles, and the merit-holder's name in order.
translations.idiomatic: On one sheet, the mobile headquarters and army commander's titles should be written prominently at the center, with the merit-holder's name in sequence.

sentences.zh: 斬三賊及被傷成階已上，亦具書於券。

translations.literal: Decapitating three bandits and being wounded to the level of one rank or more should also be fully written on the warrant.
translations.idiomatic: Decapitating three enemies and wounds qualifying for one rank or more should likewise be fully recorded on the warrant.

sentences.zh: 各盡一行，當行豎裂。

translations.literal: Each fills one line; along the line make a vertical split.
translations.idiomatic: Each entry should fill one line, with a vertical split along that line.

sentences.zh: 其券前後皆起年號日月，破某處陳，某官某勳，印記為驗。

translations.literal: At front and back of the warrant begin with reign era year, month, and day; breaking such-and-such place's formation, such-and-such official's such-and-such merit—seals as verification.
translations.idiomatic: Both ends of the warrant should bear the reign era date; breaking such-and-such enemy formation, such-and-such officer's such-and-such merit—with seals as proof.

sentences.zh: 一支付勳人，一支付行臺。

translations.literal: One copy given to the merit-holder, one given to the mobile headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: One copy goes to the merit-holder, one to the mobile headquarters.

sentences.zh: 記至京，即送門下，別函守錄。

translations.literal: When the record reaches the capital, send it immediately to the Gate Department and keep a separate sealed copy on file.
translations.idiomatic: When records reach the capital, they should go at once to the Gate Department, with a separate sealed copy kept on file.

sentences.zh: 又自遷都以來，戎車屢捷，所以征勳轉多，敍不可盡者，良由歲久生姦，積年長偽，巧吏階緣，偷增遂甚。

translations.literal: Moreover, since the move of the capital, war chariots have repeatedly won victories, so battlefield merit has steadily increased; those who cannot all be rewarded are truly because years breed fraud, long accumulation breeds falsehood, and clever clerks climb by connections, so illicit additions have become extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the capital was moved, repeated military victories have multiplied battlefield merit; the backlog of unrewarded merit owes chiefly to years of fraud, long-standing falsification, and clever clerks who exploit connections until illicit claims have grown severe.

sentences.zh: 請自今為始，諸有勳簿已經奏賞者，即廣下遠近，云某處勳判，咸令知聞。

translations.literal: I request that from now on, wherever merit registers have already been memorialized and rewarded, copies be widely sent near and far, stating such-and-such place's merit judgment, so that all may know.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that henceforth, whenever merit registers have been memorialized and rewarded, notice be sent far and wide naming the place and judgment, so that all may know.

sentences.zh: 立格酬敍，以三年為斷。

translations.literal: Establish a rule for rewarding and conferring ranks, with three years as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Set a rule that rewards must be conferred within three years.

sentences.zh: 其職人及出身，限內悉令銓除；

translations.literal: For clerical personnel and initial appointments, within the limit all are to be evaluated and cleared;
translations.idiomatic: Within that limit, clerical posts and entry-level appointments must all be filled;

sentences.zh: 實官及外號，隨才加授。

translations.literal: actual offices and external titles are to be granted according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: regular offices and honorary titles should be granted according to merit and ability.

sentences.zh: 庶使酬勤者速申，立功者勸，事不經久，僥倖易息。

translations.literal: Thus those repaying diligence may quickly report, those establishing merit may be encouraged, affairs will not drag on for long, and opportunism will easily subside.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the diligent may be rewarded promptly, men of merit encouraged, delays avoided, and opportunism easily suppressed.

sentences.zh: 或遭窮難，州無中正者，不在此限。

translations.literal: Or if they meet hardship and the province has no Rectifier of the Pure, they are outside this limit.
translations.idiomatic: Cases where hardship prevents evaluation, or a province lacks a Rectifier of the Pure, are excepted.

sentences.zh: 又勳簿之法，征還之日即應申送。

translations.literal: Moreover, by the law of merit registers, on the day the campaign returns they should be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, by merit-register law, registers should be submitted the day the army returns.

sentences.zh: 頃來行臺、督將，至京始造，或一年二歲方上勳書。

translations.literal: Recently mobile headquarters and supervising generals have waited until reaching the capital to compile them, or only after one or two years submitted merit documents.
translations.idiomatic: Recently mobile headquarters and supervising generals have waited until reaching the capital to compile registers, or submitted merit documents only after one or two years.

sentences.zh: 姦偽之原，實自由此。

translations.literal: The root of fraud and falsehood truly lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The root of fraud lies precisely here.

sentences.zh: 於今以後，軍還之日便通勳簿，不聽隔月。

translations.literal: From now on, on the day the army returns the merit register must be transmitted; crossing a month is not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth registers must be transmitted the day the army returns; delay beyond a month will not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 詔復依行。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict again ordered these measures carried out.

sentences.zh: 元叉之廢靈太后也，相州刺史、中山王熙起兵於鄴。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, the Inspector of Xiangzhou, Prince Xi of Zhongshan, raised troops at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Prince Xi of Zhongshan, who was Inspector of Xiangzhou, raised an army at Ye.

sentences.zh: 熙敗，以同為持節、兼黃門侍郎、慰勞使，乃就州刑熙。

translations.literal: When Xi was defeated, Tong was made Bearer of Credentials, concurrently Yellow Gate Attendant, and Comforting Envoy; he then executed Xi in the province.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi's defeat, Tong was appointed Bearer of Credentials and concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant as a comforting envoy; he executed Xi in the province.

sentences.zh: 還授平東將軍，正黃門，營明堂副將。

translations.literal: On his return he was given General Who Pacifies the East, Regular Yellow Gate Attendant, and Deputy Commander for constructing the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made General Who Pacifies the East, Regular Yellow Gate Attendant, and deputy commander for building the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋加撫軍將軍、光祿大夫、本州大中正。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was given the additional titles Army-soothing General, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Rectifier of the Pure for his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally named Army-soothing General, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Rectifier of the Pure for his native province.

sentences.zh: 同善事在位，為叉所親，戮熙之日，深窮黨與，以希叉旨，論者非之。

translations.literal: Tong was skilled at serving those in power and was intimate with Cha; on the day Xi was executed he pursued associates to the depths, hoping to please Cha's intent, and critics condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong knew how to please those in power and was favored by Cha; on the day Xi was killed he pursued associates relentlessly to win Cha's approval, and critics condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 又給同羽林二十人以自防衞。

translations.literal: He was also given twenty guards of the Forest of Feathers for his own protection.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted twenty guards of the Forest of Feathers for his protection.

sentences.zh: 同兄琇，少多大言，常云「公侯可致」。

translations.literal: Tong's elder brother Xiu, from youth fond of grand talk, often said, "Marquisates and dukedoms can be attained."
translations.idiomatic: Tong's elder brother Xiu had been boastful since youth, often saying that marquisates and dukedoms were within reach.

sentences.zh: 至此始為都水使者。

translations.literal: Only at this point did he become Commissioner of the Capital Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he become Commissioner of the Capital Waterways.

sentences.zh: 同啟求回身二階以加琇，琇遂除安州刺史。

translations.literal: Tong memorialized asking to return two ranks from his own person to add to Xiu; Xiu was then appointed Inspector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tong petitioned to surrender two ranks from his own record for Xiu's benefit; Xiu was then appointed Inspector of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 論者稱之。

translations.literal: Critics praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 營州城民就德興謀反，除同度支尚書，黃門如故，持節使營州慰勞，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: The city people of Yingzhou, Jiudexing, plotted rebellion; Tong was appointed Minister of the Treasury, Yellow Gate Attendant as before, bearing credentials as envoy to console Yingzhou, with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When the townspeople of Yingzhou under Jiudexing plotted rebellion, Tong was appointed Minister of the Treasury while retaining his Yellow Gate post; bearing credentials he was sent to console Yingzhou with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 同頻遣使人，皆為賊害，乃遣賊家口三十人并免家奴為良，齎書諭德興，德興乃降。

translations.literal: Tong repeatedly sent envoys, all of whom were harmed by the rebels; he then sent thirty family members of the rebels and also freed household slaves to commoner status, carrying a letter to instruct Dexing, and Dexing then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tong sent envoys repeatedly, but the rebels killed them all; he then sent thirty rebel dependents and freed household slaves to commoner status, carrying a letter to Jiudexing, who then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 安輯其民而還。

translations.literal: He settled and comforted the people and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the people and returned.

sentences.zh: 德興復反，詔同以本將軍為幽州刺史，兼尚書行臺慰勞之。

translations.literal: Dexing rebelled again; an edict made Tong, with his existing general's title, Inspector of Youzhou, concurrently Masters of Writing mobile headquarters to console them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiudexing rebelled again, Tong was ordered to serve as Inspector of Youzhou with his existing general's rank and concurrently as mobile headquarters of the Masters of Writing to console the region.

sentences.zh: 同慮德興難信，勒眾而往，為德興所擊，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Tong feared Dexing could not be trusted, drove the host forward, was struck by Dexing, suffered a great defeat, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Jiudexing could not be trusted, Tong marched in force, was attacked and routed, and retreated in defeat.

sentences.zh: 長子斐，武定中，文襄王大將軍府掾。

translations.literal: His eldest son Fei, in the Wuding era, was an aide in Grand General Wen Xiang's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fei, during the Wuding era, served as an aide in Grand General Wen Xiang Wang's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 斐弟筠，青州治中。

translations.literal: Fei's younger brother Jun was Administrative Aide of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fei's younger brother Jun served as Administrative Aide of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 同兄靜，太常丞。

translations.literal: Tong's elder brother Jing was Assistant in the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's elder brother Jing was Assistant Director of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 靜子景裕，在儒林傳。

translations.literal: Jing's son Jingyu is treated in the Confucian Scholars biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's son Jingyu is treated in the biography of Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 張烈，字徽仙，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Lie, style name Huixian, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lie, whose style name was Huixian, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 高祖賜名曰烈，仍以本名為字焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu bestowed the name Lie upon him, yet still used his original name as his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu gave him the name Lie, while his original name served as his style name.

sentences.zh: 高祖悕，為慕容 尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xi was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under the Murong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xi served the Murong as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖恂，散騎常侍，隨慕容德南渡，因居齊郡之臨淄。

translations.literal: His great-great-grandfather Xun was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, followed Murong De south across the river, and thus settled at Linzi in Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Xun was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; he followed Murong De south across the Yangzi and settled at Linzi in Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 烈少孤貧，涉獵經史，有氣概。

translations.literal: Lie from youth was orphaned and poor, ranged through the classics and histories, and had spirit and force of character.
translations.idiomatic: Lie was orphaned and poor in youth, read widely in the classics and histories, and possessed force of character.

sentences.zh: 時青州有崔徽伯、房徽叔，與烈並有令譽，時人號曰「三徽」。

translations.literal: At that time in Qingzhou were Cui Huibo and Fang Huishu; together with Lie they all had fine reputations, and men of the time called them "the Three Huis."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qingzhou had Cui Huibo and Fang Huishu; they and Lie all enjoyed fine reputations, and contemporaries called them "the Three Huis."

sentences.zh: 高祖時，入官代都，歷侍御、主文中散。

translations.literal: In Emperor Gaozu's time he entered office at the capital in Dai, passing through Attendant Censor and Regular Attendant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozu's reign he entered service at the capital in Dai, serving as Attendant Censor and Regular Attendant of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，除尚書儀曹郎、彭城王功曹史、太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he was appointed Master of Writing in the Ceremonials Bureau, Merit Officer of the Prince of Pengcheng, and Crown Prince's Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang he was appointed Master of Writing in the Ceremonials Bureau, Merit Officer to the Prince of Pengcheng, and Commandant of Footsoldiers to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶卷將陳顯達治兵漢南，謀將入寇。

translations.literal: Xiao Baojuan's general Chen Xianda drilled troops south of the Han, plotting to invade.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda, a general of Xiao Baojuan of Qi, drilled troops south of the Han and planned an invasion.

sentences.zh: 時順陽太守王青石世官江南，荊州刺史、廣陽王嘉慮其有異，表請代之。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Administrator of Shunyang, Wang Qingshi, had for generations held office south of the Yangzi; the Inspector of Jingzhou, Prince Jia of Guangyang, feared he was disloyal and memorialized requesting a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Administrator of Shunyang, Wang Qingshi, came from a family long established south of the Yangzi; Prince Jia of Guangyang, Inspector of Jingzhou, suspected his loyalty and memorialized for his replacement.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔侍臣各舉所知，互有申薦者。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the attendant ministers each to recommend men they knew, and several offered nominations.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered his attendant ministers each to recommend someone they knew, and several names were put forward.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此郡今當必爭之地，須得堪濟之才，何容汎舉也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "This commandery is now certain to become contested ground; it requires talent equal to the task—how could one put forward names at random?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "This commandery is certain to become a battleground; it requires talent equal to the task—how could one put forward names at random?

sentences.zh: 太子步兵張烈每論軍國之事，時有會人意處，朕欲用之，何如？」

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's Commandant of Footsoldiers Zhang Lie, whenever he discusses military and state affairs, often hits the point; We wish to employ him—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Commandant of Footsoldiers Zhang Lie, whenever he discusses military and state affairs, often hits the mark; I wish to employ him—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰稱贊之，遂敕除陵江將軍、順陽太守。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, praised him, and an edict thereupon appointed him General Who Crosses the Jiang and Grand Administrator of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, praised him, and an edict appointed him General Who Crosses the Jiang and Grand Administrator of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 烈到郡二日，便為寶卷將崔慧景攻圍，七十餘日，烈撫厲將士，甚得軍人之和。

translations.literal: Lie had been in the commandery two days when he was besieged by Baojuan's general Cui Huijing; for more than seventy days Lie comforted and encouraged the troops, winning great harmony among the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after Lie reached the commandery, he was besieged by Cui Huijing, a general of Xiao Baojuan; for more than seventy days Lie rallied his troops and won their wholehearted loyalty.

sentences.zh: 會車駕南討，慧景遁走。

translations.literal: It happened that the imperial carriage marched south to attack, and Huijing fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south in person, Huijing fled.

sentences.zh: 高祖親勞烈曰：「卿定可，遂能不負所寄。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu personally comforted Lie, saying, "You are certainly capable and have not failed the trust placed in you."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu personally congratulated Lie, saying, "You have proved yourself capable and have not betrayed the trust I placed in you."

sentences.zh: 烈拜謝曰：「若不值鑾輿親駕，臣將不免困於犬羊。

translations.literal: Lie bowed in thanks and said, "Had I not met the imperial carriage's personal campaign, your subject would not have escaped being trapped by dogs and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Lie bowed and replied, "Had Your Majesty not come in person, I would surely have been overrun by the enemy like a flock of beasts.

sentences.zh: 自是陛下不負臣，非臣能不負陛下。」

translations.literal: From this it is Your Majesty who has not failed your subject, not that your subject could fail to fail Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: It is Your Majesty who has not failed me—not that I could claim never to have failed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 高祖善其對。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，追錄先勳，封清河縣開國子，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he recorded former merit and enfeoffed him as Viscount Who Founded the State of Qinghe, with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he recognized Lie's earlier merit and enfeoffed him as founding viscount of Qinghe County with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老歸養。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because his mother was old, he returned home to support her.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired to care for his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，頻值凶儉，烈為粥以食飢人，蒙濟者甚眾，鄉黨以此稱之。

translations.literal: Over more than ten years he frequently met with famine and dearth; Lie made gruel to feed the hungry, and those who received relief were very many; his village and district praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he lived through repeated famines; Lie made gruel to feed the hungry, relieving a great many people, and his neighbors praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，除龍驤將軍、司徒右長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign he was appointed Dragon Cavalry General and Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Suzong's reign he was appointed Dragon Cavalry General and Right Chief Clerk under the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 又轉征虜將軍、司空長史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians and Chief Clerk under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 先是，元叉父江陽王繼曾為青州刺史，及叉當權，烈託故義之懷，遂相諂附。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan Cha's father Prince Ji of Jiangyang had once been Inspector of Qingzhou; when Cha held power, Lie relied on their old bond of righteousness and thus flattered and attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan Cha's father, Prince Ji of Jiangyang, had served as Inspector of Qingzhou; when Cha came to power, Lie invoked their old ties and attached himself to him with flattery.

sentences.zh: 除前將軍、給事黃門侍郎，尋加平南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Forward General and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and shortly given the additional titles General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Forward General and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and soon additionally named General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 後靈太后反政，以烈叉黨，出為鎮東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, when Empress Dowager Ling regained power, because Lie was counted among Cha's faction, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling later regained power, Lie was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qingzhou because he was counted among Cha's faction.

sentences.zh: 于時議者以烈家產畜殖，僮客甚多，慮其怨望，不宜出為本州，改授安北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time critics, because Lie's household wealth and livestock had multiplied and his retainers were many, feared he harbored resentment and that he should not be sent out to his home province; he was instead given General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics at the time noted that Lie's household wealth and retinue had grown large and feared he might harbor resentment if sent to his home province; he was instead appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，吏民安之。

translations.literal: His governance was pure and tranquil, and officials and people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was quiet and orderly, and officials and commoners alike were content.

sentences.zh: 更滿還朝，因辭老還鄉里。

translations.literal: When his term ended he returned to court, then citing old age went back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he returned to court, then retired to his home district on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同居怡怡然，為親類所慕。

translations.literal: The brothers lived together in easy contentment and were admired by kin.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers lived together in harmony and were admired by their kin.

sentences.zh: 元象元年，卒於家，時年七十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he died at home, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanxiang era he died at home at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 烈先為家誡千餘言，并自敍志行及所歷之官，臨終敕子姪不聽求贈，但勒家誡立碣而已。

translations.literal: Lie had earlier written more than a thousand words of family admonitions and also narrated his aims, conduct, and offices held; on his deathbed he ordered his sons and nephews not to seek posthumous honors, but only to inscribe the family admonitions on a stele.
translations.idiomatic: Lie had earlier composed more than a thousand words of family admonitions and recorded his aims, conduct, and offices; on his deathbed he forbade his sons and nephews to seek posthumous honors and asked only that the admonitions be carved on a stele.

sentences.zh: 其子質奉行焉。

translations.literal: His son Zhi carried this out.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi obeyed these instructions.

sentences.zh: 質，博學多才藝。

translations.literal: Zhi was broadly learned and skilled in many arts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was learned and gifted in many arts.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請，員外郎、龍驤將軍、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On leaving the cloth he became Court Gentleman for Attendance, Extraordinary Master of Writing, Dragon Cavalry General, and Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he served as Court Gentleman for Attendance, Extraordinary Master of Writing, Dragon Cavalry General, and Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 未襲爵。

translations.literal: He did not inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He did not inherit his father's title.

sentences.zh: 興和中，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era he died at home.

sentences.zh: 質弟登，州主簿。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Deng was Provincial Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Deng served as Provincial Recorder.

sentences.zh: 烈弟僧晧，字山客。

translations.literal: Lie's younger brother Senghao, style name Shanke.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's younger brother Senghao, whose style name was Shanke.

sentences.zh: 歷涉羣書，工於談說，有名於當世。

translations.literal: He ranged through many books, was skilled at discourse, and had a name in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, excelled at conversation, and enjoyed a reputation in his day.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，徵為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping he was summoned as Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xiping reign he was summoned as Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，以國子博士徵之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengguang he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengguang he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，徵為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang he was summoned as Attendant Cavalryman.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaochang he was summoned as Attendant Cavalryman.

sentences.zh: 並不赴。

translations.literal: He did not go to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: He declined every summons.

sentences.zh: 世號為徵君焉。

translations.literal: His age called him the Recluse Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries called him the Recluse Lord.

sentences.zh: 好營產業，孜孜不已，藏鏹巨萬，他資亦稱是。

translations.literal: He loved building up estates and worked tirelessly without cease; his stored cash amounted to tens of thousands, and his other assets were comparable.
translations.idiomatic: He loved amassing property and worked tirelessly; his hoarded cash ran to tens of thousands, with other assets to match.

sentences.zh: 兄弟自供儉約，車馬瘦弊，身服布裳，而婢妾紈綺。

translations.literal: The brothers themselves lived frugally; their carriages and horses were lean and worn, they wore cloth garments, yet their maidservants and concubines wore silk brocades.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers lived frugally themselves—their carriages and horses were shabby, they wore plain cloth, yet their maidservants and concubines dressed in silk brocade.

sentences.zh: 僧晧尤好蒲弈，戲不擇人，是以獲譏於世。

translations.literal: Senghao especially loved playing bo, and in play did not choose his opponents, for which he was mocked by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Senghao was especially fond of playing bo and would play with anyone, for which he was ridiculed.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時，崔祖螭舉兵攻東陽城，僧晧與同。

translations.literal: In the time of the Deposed Former Emperor, Cui Zuchi raised troops and attacked Dongyang city; Senghao joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Deposed Former Emperor, when Cui Zuchi raised troops against Dongyang, Senghao joined the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事敗，死於獄，籍沒家產。

translations.literal: When the affair failed he died in prison and his household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot failed he died in prison and his estate was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，訴復業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign, through appeal his estate was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Chu's reign his family appealed and recovered their property.

sentences.zh: 子軌，州主簿。

translations.literal: His son Gui was Provincial Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui served as Provincial Recorder.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：盧同質器洪厚，卷舒兼濟。

translations.literal: The historian says: Lu Tong's native substance was broad and deep, able both to advance and to withdraw as the times required.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Lu Tong possessed a broad and weighty character, able to adapt whether advancing or withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 張烈早標名輩，氣尚見知。

translations.literal: Zhang Lie early marked himself among famous men, and his spirit and bearing won recognition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lie early distinguished himself among notable men, and his bearing won esteem.

sentences.zh: 趨捨深沉，俱至顯達，雅道正路，其殆病諸。

translations.literal: Their choices in advance and retreat were deep and hidden; both reached eminence—yet on the refined path and upright road, this is perhaps where they fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Both pursued their ambitions with subtle calculation and reached high office—yet on the path of true refinement, this may be where they fell short.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 郎中別作抄目 諸本「目」訛「自」，不可通，今據北史卷三０盧同傳改。

translations.literal: On "the director shall make a separate copy register": in various editions "register" (mu) is wrongly written as "self" (zi), which makes no sense; the text is now corrected according to the biography of Lu Tong in juan 30 of the History of the Northern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "the director shall make a separate copy register": various editions wrongly read "register" (mu) as "self" (zi), which is unintelligible; the text is corrected here according to Lu Tong's biography in juan 30 of the History of the Northern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 臣頃奏以黃素為勳 按「勳」下當脫「簿」字，下云「黃素勳簿」可證。

translations.literal: On "Your subject recently memorialized using yellow plain silk for merit": under "merit" the character "register" (bu) is missing; the phrase "yellow plain silk merit register" below proves this.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "I recently memorialized using yellow plain silk for merit": the word "register" (bu) is missing after "merit," as shown by the phrase "yellow merit register" below.

sentences.zh: 節度大都督李叔仁

translations.literal: Grand Commander-in-Chief and Controller Li Shuren
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander-in-Chief and Controller Li Shuren

translations.literal: 〈Missing〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Missing text〉

sentences.zh: 諸本下旁注「闕」字。

translations.literal: Various editions have a marginal note reading "missing."
translations.idiomatic: Various editions carry a marginal note reading "missing."

sentences.zh: 按卷九肅宗紀孝昌三年二月庚申稱東郡民趙顯德反，詔都督李叔仁討之；

translations.literal: According to juan 9 of the Annals of Emperor Suzong, in the third year of Xiaochang, second month, day gengshen, it says the people of Dong Commandery under Zhao Xiande rebelled and an edict ordered Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 9 of Emperor Suzong's annals, on gengshen day in the second month of the third year of Xiaochang, the people of Dong Commandery under Zhao Xiande rebelled, and an edict ordered Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren to suppress them;

sentences.zh: 三月辛未又稱齊州廣川民劉鈞執清河太守邵懷聚眾反，六月稱詔都督李叔仁討劉鈞平之。

translations.literal: third month, day xinwei, it again says the people of Guangchuan in Qizhou, Liu Jun, seized the Grand Administrator of Qinghe, Shao Huai, gathered a host and rebelled; sixth month says an edict ordered Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren to attack Liu Jun and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: on xinwei day in the third month it records that Liu Jun of Guangchuan in Qizhou seized Grand Administrator Shao Huai of Qinghe and raised a rebellion; in the sixth month an edict ordered Commander-in-Chief Li Shuren to attack Liu Jun and pacify him.

sentences.zh: 東郡屬西兗州。

translations.literal: Dong Commandery belonged to West Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Commandery belonged to West Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 盧同以齊兗二州行臺節度李叔仁，所闕必即鎮壓這兩支變亂軍事，但紀不書盧同以行臺節度事。

translations.literal: Lu Tong, as mobile headquarters of Qi and Yanzhou, controlled Li Shuren; what is missing must be the suppression of these two rebellions, yet the annals do not record Lu Tong's role as mobile headquarters controller.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong, as mobile headquarters over Qi and the two Yanzhou provinces, directed Li Shuren; the missing passage must concern the suppression of these two rebellions, though the annals do not record Tong's role as mobile headquarters commander.
